acceptance_criteria.criterion: One active primary membership per organization/person is enforced under concurrency
evidence: executed:supabase/tests/wfc004_workforce_departments.harness.sh stage 3a. Two simultaneous psql sessions inserted a PRIMARY membership for the same (organization, person) into two DIFFERENT departments: exactly 1 row resulted and at least one 23505 named workforce_department_memberships_one_active_primary_uidx. THE CONTROL: with the index DROPPED, the same two concurrent inserts BOTH succeeded - so the claim is a measurement of that index and not of a coincidence. The same construction and the same drop-the-index control are applied to workforce_department_managers_one_accountable_uidx in stage 3b. The contract postflight asserts the index's WHERE clause, not merely its existence, because an index that silently lost its predicate stops being a guarantee while still being present.

Preserved v1 criterion metadata: {"how":"workforce_department_memberships_one_active_primary_uidx is a PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEX on (org_id, person_user_id) where membership_kind='primary' and is_active and effective_to is null - an index, not a trigger, because an index is what the database enforces under concurrency.","stated_limit":"'At most one' is enforced. 'At least one' is a property of a SET of rows and is NOT enforced - demoting the last active primary to secondary would leave a worker with none. It is DETECTED by public.workforce_membership_health and prevented at WFC-005's command layer. A deferred cross-row constraint trigger was considered and rejected: it would fire on every membership write including bulk imports."}

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Secondary memberships do not change primary membership or authority
evidence: executed: stage 3e. POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST: the appointed manager of the department IS resolved, so the denials are not vacuous. A worker whose only relationship is a SECONDARY membership resolves to FALSE; their UPDATE affects 0 rows and exits 0 (the silent-no-op fact, CP-114); their self-appointment INSERT is refused 42501; their ledger INSERT naming their own membership is refused 42501; and a manager of department A cannot place a membership into department B, with check being evaluated against the department_id being WRITTEN. THE FUNCTIONS BODY is proven by the contract postflight check department_scope_reads_memberships, and the harness INJECTS the widening edit - adding the memberships table to the function - and requires the postflight to report it, then removes it and requires green again.

Preserved v1 criterion metadata: {"how":"THREE structural facts, each independently assertable and none of them prose. (a) public.workforce_department_is_managed_by is the only department-scope predicate any policy or view uses, and its body reads workforce_department_managers and NEVER workforce_department_memberships. (b) The manager relation's INSERT and UPDATE require organization-wide workforce.manage, which DB-016 deliberately does NOT grant to department_manager, so a worker cannot promote themselves by writing a row. (c) Neither the manager nor the membership relation has a DELETE policy or a DELETE privilege, for authenticated, anon AND service_role.","corrections_this_criterion_needed":"The first revision asserted on the psql exit code and reported two rc=0 'failures' that were both SUCCESSES - the silent-no-op finding, now CP-114 and HF-WFC-004-AFFECTED-ROW-COUNT. The checks were rewritten to count affected rows and to pair every 0-row result with the 1-row result for a different caller."}

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cross-organization manager, vendor, worker, and department references fail
evidence: executed: stage 3g. Six cross-organization refusals, EACH PAIRED WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL using the identical statement at the correct org_id, and each asserted by CONSTRAINT NAME so a refusal for the wrong reason is visible: 23503 on workforce_department_managers_department_fkey, on the vendor-kind FK, on the membership department FK, on the ledger's three-column membership FK, on the alias FK, and on the ledger's cross-scope supersedes FK. The first attempt at the manager case measured 23505 on the one-accountable-manager index instead of 23503 - a real refusal for the wrong reason - and a department with no open manager was used so the tenant check is what answers. Separately an org B administrator reads 0 of org A's departments through RLS, and an org A administrator - holding organization-wide authority - STILL cannot appoint a manager of org B's department, because the composite FK binds the two columns.

Preserved v1 criterion metadata: {"how":"COMPOSITE FOREIGN KEYS, not policy denials, so the references are structurally impossible rather than merely refused: (vendor_entity_id, org_id) -> vendor_entities(id, org_id); (department_id, org_id) -> workforce_departments(id, org_id) on managers, memberships AND the ledger; (membership_id, department_id, person_user_id) -> memberships, a THREE-column key; (supersedes_event_id, org_id, department_id) on the ledger; (vendor_id, org_id) on aliases; and (merged_into_id, org_id) on the vendor master, so a merge cannot cross a tenant either.","instrument_note":"The contract postflight asserts these foreign keys by name AND asserts that each is COMPOSITE, by column count, because a single-column FK with the same name would satisfy an existence check while permitting exactly the cross-tenant reference the name promises to forbid."}

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Backfill is idempotent and unresolved records remain explicitly reviewable
evidence: executed: stage 4. THE BACKFILL IS MEASURED NOT TO REPLACE: re-applying over two free-text department strings, one org-less staff row, one name-only vendor contract, one name-only event request, one tour-scoped vendor and one tenant-less staffing agency created ZERO departments and ZERO memberships and produced 14 link rows and 13 quarantine rows. IDEMPOTENCY IS A COUNT, NOT AN INTENTION: a third apply left both counts identical. REVIEWABILITY IS ASSERTED PER CLASSIFICATION: all thirteen expected (subject_table, quarantine_code) pairs are present by name - department_not_an_entity, vendor_identity_name_only on four tables, org_key_missing, org_key_cross_tenant_only, and vendor_table_unproven on all six chain-absent reader relations. Every link row carries non-empty EVIDENCE rather than only a verdict, and the free-text department observation records the row count it was derived from. THE VISIBILITY SPLIT IS CORRECT AND MEASURED: an org administrator sees 2 of 14 link rows, because rows whose subject has no established organization (staffing_agencies has no tenant column at all) are invisible to every authenticated caller by design, and the operator is pointed at workforce_reconciliation_audit rather than at a policy to widen.

Preserved v1 criterion metadata: {"how":"Eleven backfill statements, each guarded by `on conflict ... do update ... where <is distinct from>` or `on conflict do nothing`, over a unique key on (subject_table, coalesce(subject_id::text, subject_key)). The two reconciliation tables are constrained so an unresolved row MUST carry a WORKFORCE_QUARANTINE_CODES code and non-empty evidence, a linked row must name a target, and a resolved quarantine must state resolved_at, resolved_by AND a note of at least three characters.","why_no_backfill_of_departments_or_memberships":"Because there is NO provable source. The only department-bearing column in the chain is unconstrained nullable TEXT with no foreign key, and WFC-003 §6.9 requires the department entity to replace every free-text column by explicit LINK, never by value comparison. Creating a department named after a string and attaching people to it by matching that string is the merge CP-096 forbids and the resolution that would manufacture the authority the new schema exists to stop inventing."}
